title: Harmony of All Religions (Sarvadharma Samanvaya)
author: Sant Sevi Ji Maharaj (1920-2007)
edition_cited: Santmat Society of North America, first English edition (201 copies), copyright 2003 and 2006; archive.org item HarmonyOfAllReligions
locator_hints: File c. 1425-1500 (introduction to the four practices): drishti yoga as gazing on a single infinitesimal point between the eyebrows; 'advised neither to focus forcefully nor manipulate the eyeballs'

summary: Sant Sevi, Mehi's successor, restates the Santmat practice inside a survey of Vedic, Jain, Buddhist, Christian, Islamic and Sikh sources. The practical passages describe what is met on closing the eyes (darkness, identified as the realm one must first leave) and the method for leaving it: after mantra and form meditation, gaze on a single infinitesimal point in the middle of the inner darkness between the eyebrows, without forcing the focus or manipulating the eyeballs; when the practitioner is established in focusing 'the beams of both eyes' on one point, a bright bindu emerges; Mehi is quoted as saying bindu and sound 'will come and receive you'. He equates this 'focused gazing' with practices named in the Upanishads and with Jain preksha dhyana, and, for the sound stage, criticises systems that press the ears with the hands. Slower and more discursive than Mehi's manual but adds explanation and the lineage's comparative claims.
why_relevant: Second teacher-level statement of the drishti-yoga route to first light, with explicit prohibition of eyeball manipulation and a description of how the bright point emerges.
